newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA LISTED SANEVIT ANNOUNCES 12 BLN LEI DEAL.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA LISTED SANEVIT ANNOUNCES 12 BLN LEI DEAL.

text.p: Romanian listed syringe maker Sanevit SA said on Tuesday it had struck a 12 billion lei deal with the Health Ministry to supply disposable syringes.

"Syringe deliveries, meant for health units coordinated by the ministry, cover the first quarter of 1997," Sanevit's Felicia Cruceanu said from the company's headquarters in the Transylvanian city of Arad.
Sanevit, Romania's sole producer of disposable syringes, plans an output of 125 million syringes and 390 million needles this year.

The company started production in April 1995 with a targeted annual output of 180 million syringes and 400 million needles. The domestic market can absorb up to 300 million syringes and 400 million needles a year.
Cruceanu said a shareholders' meeting later this month would agree on increasing Sanevit's share capital, now standing at 24.7 billion lei, by adding imported equipment.
The equipment -- bought from Italy's Penta Group on a $37 million credit guaranteed by the Romanian state -- was assessed by accountants Coopers and Lybrand.
At the latest trading session last Thursday Sanevit closed at 12,500 lei, 500 lei weaker on the week.
Its peak closing price was 71,000 lei in November 1995, soon after the Bucharest stock exchange had opened. ($=7,744 lei)
